translations.text: After Moses, the servant of the Lord, died, the Lord said to Joshua son of Nun, Moses’ assistant:
“Moses my servant is dead. Now get up and cross this Jordan, you and all these people, into the land that I am giving them, the Israelites.
Every place where the sole of your foot treads will be yours, as I told Moses.
Your territory will extend from the wilderness and this Mount Lebanon to the Euphrates, the great river, and through all the land of the Hittites as far as the Great Sea in the west.
No one will stand against you all the days of your lives. Just as I was with Moses, I will also be with you. I will not abandon you or leave you.
Be strong and very courageous, because you will give these people as their inheritance the land that I swore to their ancestors to give them.

Only be strong and very courageous in keeping and carrying out all the laws that Moses my servant commanded you. Do not turn aside from them, either to the right or to the left, so that you may succeed wherever you go.
This book of the law must not leave your mouth. Instead, meditate on it night and day, and keep and carry out everything written in it, so that you may prosper and succeed.
Look, I have commanded you: be strong and courageous. Do not be afraid or tremble, because the Lord your God is with you wherever you go.”
Joshua commanded the leaders of the people and their scribes, saying to them:

“Go through the camp and command the people, telling them, ‘Prepare provisions for yourselves, because in three days you will cross this Jordan to enter and take possession of the land that the Lord your God is giving you to possess.’”
Joshua said to Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh:
“Remember the command that Moses, the servant of the Lord, gave you when he said to you, ‘The Lord your God is giving you rest and is giving you this land.’

Your wives, your households, and your livestock will remain in the land that Moses gave you beyond the Jordan. But you, all your mighty warriors, must cross over armed ahead of your brothers and help them,

until the Lord gives your brothers rest as he has given you, and they too possess the land that the Lord your God is giving them. Then you may return to the land of your inheritance and possess it, the land that Moses, the servant of the Lord, gave you beyond the Jordan toward the sunrise.”
The descendants of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh answered Joshua, saying, “We will do everything you command us, and we will go wherever you send us.
Just as we obeyed Moses, so we will obey you. Only may the Lord your God be with you as he was with Moses.
Anyone who opposes you and does not obey your word in everything you command him will be put to death. Only be strong and courageous.”

Joshua son of Nun sent two men familiar with the land from Shittim and told them, “Go and inspect the land of Jericho.” They went and entered the house of a prostitute named Rahab and spent the night there.
The king of Jericho was told, “Look, men from the Israelites have come here tonight to spy out the land.”
The king of Jericho sent word to Rahab, saying to her, “Bring out the men who came to you tonight, because they have come to spy out our land.”
The woman took the two men and hid them. She said, “The men did indeed come to me, but I did not know where they were from.
When it was time to shut the gate in the evening, they left, and I do not know where they went. Go after them quickly, because you can catch up with them.”
But she had taken them up to the roof and hidden them among the stalks of flax that she had laid out on the roof.
The men went after them along the road to the Jordan, toward the ford. The gate was shut after the pursuers had gone out after those spies.
They had not yet lain down when she went up to them on the roof.
She said to the men, “I know that the Lord has given you the land. Fear of you has fallen upon us, and all the inhabitants of the land are afraid of you.
For we have heard that the Lord dried up the waters of the Red Sea before you when you came out of Egypt, and what you did to the two kings of the Amorites, Sihon and Og, whom you destroyed.
When we heard, our hearts trembled, and no spirit remained in any of us because of you, for the Lord your God is God in heaven above and on earth below.
Now swear to me by the Lord, since I have shown you kindness, that you too will show kindness to me and my father’s household. Give me a trustworthy sign,
and spare my father, my mother, my brothers, my sisters, and everyone belonging to us, and save our lives from death.”
The men said to her, “We pledge our own lives to death in place of yours, provided you do not reveal this matter. When the Lord gives us this land, we will treat you with kindness and faithfulness.”
She lowered them by a rope through the window, because her house was in the city wall, and she lived on the wall.
She said to them, “Go into the hills [?], so that those who went out after you do not encounter you. Hide there for three days, until they return, and then go on your way.”
The men said to her, “We are free from this oath that you have made us swear.

Look, when we enter the land, tie this scarlet cord in the window through which you lowered us, and bring your father, your mother, your brothers, and your father’s entire household into the house with you.

Anyone who goes outside through the door of your house will have his blood on his own head, and we will be free of responsibility for him. But anyone who is with you inside the house will have his blood on our heads, and we will be responsible for him if anyone harms him.
If you reveal this matter, we will be free from the oath that you have made us swear.”
She said to them, “Let it be as you have said.” She sent them away, and they left. Then she tied the scarlet cord in the window.

They went into the hills and stayed there for three days, until those who had gone after them returned to the town. Those who had gone out after them searched for them along the entire road, and when they did not find them,
they returned. The two spies came down from the hills, crossed over, and went to Joshua son of Nun. They told him everything that had happened to them.
They said to Joshua, “The Lord has handed the whole land over to us, and all the inhabitants of the land are afraid of us.”
Joshua rose early in the morning, and they set out from Shittim. All the people of Israel came to the Jordan and spent the night there without crossing.
After three days, the officers went through the camp.
They gave the people these instructions: “When you see the ark of the covenant of the Lord your God, and the priests and Levites carrying it, set out from where you are and follow it.
But keep a distance of about two thousand cubits between yourselves and the ark. Do not come near it, so that you may know the way you should go, because you have never traveled this way before.”
Joshua said to the people, “Make yourselves holy, because tomorrow the Lord will do wonders among you.”
Joshua said to the priests, “Pick up the ark of the covenant and go ahead of the people.” They picked up the ark of the covenant and went ahead of the people.
The Lord said to Joshua, “Beginning today, I will make you great in the eyes of all Israel, so that they may know that just as I was with Moses, I will also be with you.
Command the priests carrying the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and tell them, ‘When you reach the edge of the waters of the Jordan, stand in the Jordan itself.’”
Joshua said to the Israelites, “Come here and hear the words of the Lord your God.”
Joshua said, “By this you will know that the living God is among you and will destroy before you the Hittites, Canaanites, Hivites, Perizzites, Girgashites, Amorites, and Jebusites.
Look, the ark of the covenant of the Lord, the Lord of the whole earth, is ahead of you in the Jordan.
Now choose twelve men for yourselves from all the tribes of Israel, one man from each tribe.

When the soles of the feet of the priests carrying the ark of the covenant of the Lord, the Lord of the whole earth, rest in the waters of the Jordan, the waters of the Jordan will divide. The waters coming down from above will stand on one side, as though in a single waterskin.”
When the people set out from their tents to cross the Jordan, the priests carrying the ark of the covenant went ahead of the people.
When those carrying the ark reached the Jordan, the feet of the priests carrying the ark dipped into the water at its edge. The Jordan was full from bank to bank throughout the harvest season.

The waters coming down from above stopped. They stood on one side, as though in a single waterskin, extending very far away from Aram, the town beside Zarethan. The waters flowing down to the western sea, the Salt Sea, ran out and were cut off. The people crossed opposite Jericho.

The priests carrying the ark of the covenant of the Lord stood on dry ground in the middle of the Jordan. All the house of Israel made ready and crossed on dry ground, until all the people had finished crossing the Jordan.
When all the people had finished crossing the Jordan, the Lord said to Joshua,
“Choose twelve men for yourselves from the people, one man from each tribe.”

He commanded them, saying, “Take stones for yourselves from here, from the middle of the Jordan, from beneath the priests’ feet. Prepare twelve stones, carry them across with you, and place them where you will spend the night.”
Joshua called the twelve men whom they had selected from the Israelites, one man from each tribe.
Joshua said to them, “Go ahead of the ark of the Lord your God into the middle of the Jordan, and let each man put a stone on his shoulder, according to the number of the tribes of the Israelites.
This will be a sign among you. When your children ask you in the future, ‘What are these stones?’

tell them, ‘The waters of the Jordan divided before the ark of the covenant of the Lord. When we crossed the Jordan, the waters of the Jordan divided.’ These stones will be a memorial for the Israelites forever.”

The Israelites did as Joshua commanded them. They took twelve stones from the middle of the Jordan, as the Lord had told Joshua, according to the number of the tribes of the Israelites. They carried them across with them to the place where they would spend the night and left them there.
They set up twelve stones that they had taken from the middle of the Jordan, from beneath the feet of the priests carrying the ark of the covenant. They remain there to this day.

The priests carrying the ark stood in the middle of the Jordan until everything the Lord had commanded Joshua to tell the people had been carried out, just as Moses had commanded Joshua. The people hurried across.
When all the people had completely crossed over, the ark of the Lord and the priests crossed over ahead of the people.
The Reubenites, the Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh crossed over armed ahead of the Israelites, as Moses had told them.
Forty thousand armed men crossed over before the Lord for battle on the plain of Jericho.
On that day the Lord made Joshua great in the eyes of all Israel, and they revered him as they had revered Moses, all the days of his life.
The Lord said to Joshua,
“Command the priests carrying the ark of the testimony to come up out of the Jordan.”
Joshua commanded the priests, saying to them, “Come up out of the Jordan.”

When the priests carrying the ark of the covenant of the Lord came up out of the Jordan, the soles of their feet touched dry ground. The waters of the Jordan returned to their place and flowed over all its banks as before.
The people came up out of the Jordan on the tenth day of the first month and camped at Gilgal, on the eastern outskirts of Jericho.
Joshua set up at Gilgal the twelve stones they had taken from the middle of the Jordan.
He said to the Israelites, “When your children ask you in the future, ‘What are these stones?’
show them to your children and tell them, ‘The Israelites crossed this Jordan on dry ground.’
The Lord your God dried up the waters of the Jordan before them until they had crossed, just as the Lord your God did to the Red Sea, which he dried up before us until we had crossed,
so that all the peoples of the earth might know that the Lord’s hand is mighty, and so that you might fear the Lord your God all your days.”

When all the kings of the Amorites west of the Jordan and all the kings of Canaan along the sea heard that the Lord had dried up the waters of the Jordan before the Israelites until they had crossed, their hearts trembled, and they had no courage left because of the Israelites.
At that time the Lord said to Joshua, “Make yourself a flint knife and circumcise the Israelites again, a second time.”
Joshua made himself a flint knife and circumcised the Israelites a second time at the Hill of the Foreskins.
These are the ones Joshua circumcised: all the male offspring of the people who had come out of Egypt, because all the fighting men had died in the wilderness along the way after coming out of Egypt.
For all the people who came out had been circumcised, but none of the people born in the wilderness along the way after they came out of Egypt had been circumcised.

For the Israelites traveled in the wilderness for forty years, until all the fighting men who had come out of Egypt had perished, because they had not obeyed the Lord their God. The Lord swore to them that he would not let them see the land he had sworn to their ancestors to give them, a land flowing with milk and honey.
Joshua circumcised their sons who came after them, because they were uncircumcised and had not been circumcised.
When all the people had finished being circumcised, they stayed in their places in the camp until they had healed.
The Lord said to Joshua, “Today I have removed the disgrace of the Egyptians from you.” He named that place Gilgal, and that is its name to this day.
The Israelites camped at Gilgal and celebrated the Passover on the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month, in the plain of Jericho.
After the Passover they ate some of the grain of the land. On that very day they ate unleavened bread and roasted grain.
The manna ceased the following day, after they had eaten some of the grain of the land. There was no more manna for the Israelites, and that year they ate the produce of the land of Canaan.
When Joshua was in the plain of Jericho, he looked up and saw a man standing opposite him, holding a drawn sword in his hand. Joshua went to him and said, “Are you one of us or one of our enemies?”
He said to him, “I am the commander of the Lord’s armies, and now I have come.” Joshua fell facedown on the ground and bowed in worship. He said, “What does my lord say to his servant?”
The commander of the Lord’s armies said to Joshua, “Take your sandals off your feet, because the place where you are standing is holy.” Joshua did so.
Jericho was shut up because of the Israelites. No one went out, and no one came in.
The Lord said to Joshua, “See, I have handed Jericho over to you, along with its king and its entire army.
Surround the city, all you fighting men, and march around the city once each day. Do this for six days.”
Seven priests shall carry horns and sound them before the ark. On the seventh day, go around the city seven times, and the priests shall blow the horns.
When they sound the horns and you hear the sound of the horn, all the people shall give a great shout. The city wall will fall where it stands, and the people shall go up, each straight ahead.
Joshua son of Nun called the priests and said to them, “Carry the ark of the Lord’s covenant, and let seven priests carry seven horns and sound them before the ark of the Lord.”
He said to the people, “Go forward and march around the city, and let those who are armed go ahead of the ark of the Lord.”

As Joshua had told the people, seven priests were carrying seven horns and sounding them before the ark of the Lord. They were blowing the horns, and the ark of the Lord’s covenant was following them.
The armed men went ahead of the priests who were blowing the horns, and the rear guard went behind the ark. They marched along, blowing the horns.
Joshua commanded the people, saying, “Do not shout or let your voices be heard. Do not let a word come out of your mouths until the day I tell you to shout. Then you shall shout.”
The ark of the Lord went around the city once. Then they returned to the camp and spent the night there.
Joshua rose early in the morning, and the priests took up the ark of the Lord.

Seven priests carrying seven horns went ahead of the ark of the Lord, marching along and blowing the horns. The armed men went ahead of them, and the rear guard went behind the ark of the Lord, with the horns being blown.
On the second day they marched around that city once and returned to the camp. They did this for all six days.
On the seventh day they rose early in the morning and marched around the city seven times in this same manner. Only on that day did they march around it seven times.
On the seventh time, the priests blew the horns, and Joshua said to the people, “Shout, for the Lord has handed the city over to you!
This city and everything in it shall be devoted to destruction for the Lord. Spare only Rahab the prostitute and everyone with her in the house, because she hid the spies we sent.
But you must be careful to keep away from what is devoted to destruction, so that you do not secretly take any of it and make the camp of Israel subject to destruction and bring trouble upon it.
All the silver and gold, and the bronze and iron objects, are holy to the Lord. They shall go into the Lord’s treasury.”

The people shouted, and the horns were blown. When the people heard the sound of the horns, they gave an exceedingly loud shout, and the wall collapsed where it stood. The people went up into the city, each straight ahead, and captured it.
They destroyed everything in it—men and women, young and old, cattle, sheep, and donkeys—with the edge of the sword.
Joshua said to the two men who had spied out the land, “Go into the prostitute’s house and bring the woman out of there, along with all that belongs to her, just as you swore to her.”
The spies went and brought out Rahab, her father, her mother, her brothers, and all that belonged to her. They brought out her entire family and settled them outside the camp of Israel.
They burned the city and everything in it with fire. Only the gold, silver, and bronze and iron objects did they bring into the Lord’s treasury.
But Joshua spared Rahab the prostitute, her father’s household, and all that belonged to her. She has lived among the Israelites to this day, because she hid the spies Joshua sent to spy out Jericho.

At that time Joshua pronounced an oath, saying, “Cursed before the Lord is the man who rises up and rebuilds this city, Jericho. At the cost of his firstborn he shall build it, and at the cost of his youngest he shall erect its gates.”
The Lord was with Joshua, and his fame spread throughout the land.

The Israelites acted unfaithfully concerning what was devoted to destruction. Achar son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, from the tribe of Judah, took some of what was devoted to destruction and hid it. The Lord’s anger burned against the Israelites.
Joshua sent men from Jericho to Ai, which is beside Beth-aven, east of Bethel. He told them, “Go up and spy out the land.” So the men went up and spied out Ai.
They returned to Joshua and said to him, “Do not let all the people go up. Let about two or three thousand men go up and destroy Ai. Do not send all the people, because they are few.”
About three thousand men from the people went up there, but they fled before the men of Ai.
The men of Ai killed thirty-six men of Israel. They pursued them from the gate until they were defeated and struck them down. The people’s courage shook, and they became like water.
Joshua tore his clothes and fell facedown on the ground before the ark of the Lord until evening, he and the elders of Israel. They put dust on their heads.
Joshua said, “Alas, Lord God, why did you bring this people across the Jordan, only to hand us over to the Amorites? If only we had been content to stay on the other side of the Jordan!
What can I say now that Israel has turned its back before its enemies?
The Canaanites and all the inhabitants of the land will hear about it. They will gather against us and wipe out our name from the face of the earth. What, then, will you do for your great name?”
The Lord said to Joshua, “Get up! Why are you lying face down on the ground?
Israel has sinned. They have broken the command I gave them and taken some of the things set apart for destruction. They have also stolen, lied, and hidden them among their belongings.

The Israelites will no longer be able to stand against their enemies. Instead, they will turn their backs before their enemies, because they themselves have become set apart for destruction. I will no longer be with them unless you remove the things set apart for destruction from among you.

Get up, prepare this people, and say, ‘Prepare yourselves for tomorrow, because this is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: There are things set apart for destruction among you, Israel. You can no longer stand against your enemies until you remove the things set apart for destruction from among you.’

In the morning, bring your tribes forward. The tribe that the Lord selects shall come forward clan by clan. The clan that the Lord selects shall come forward household by household, and the household that the Lord selects shall come forward man by man.
The one who is caught with the things set apart for destruction shall be burned with fire, he and everything he has, because he has broken the Lord’s command and committed wrongdoing in Israel.”
Joshua rose early in the morning and brought Israel forward tribe by tribe, and the tribe of Judah was selected.
He brought the tribe of Judah forward clan by clan, and the clan of Zerah was selected. He brought the clan of Zerah forward household by household, and Zabdi was selected.
He brought his household forward man by man, and Achar son of Carmi, son of Zabdi, son of Zerah, from the tribe of Judah, was selected.
Joshua said to Achar, “Give glory to the Lord, the God of Israel, and make confession to him. Tell me what you have done, and do not hide it from me.”
Achar answered Joshua, “Truly, I have sinned against the Lord, the God of Israel. This is what I did:

Among the plunder I saw a Babylonian cloak—it was beautiful—and two hundred shekels of silver and a gold bar weighing fifty shekels. I coveted them and took them. They are now buried in the ground inside my tent, with the silver underneath.”
Joshua sent men, and they ran to his tent. They saw that the things were buried in his tent, with the silver underneath.
They took them from his tent and brought them to Joshua and to all Israel, and he placed them before the Lord.

Joshua took Achar son of Zerah, along with the silver, the cloak, and the gold bar. He took his sons, his daughters, his oxen, his donkey, his flock, his tent, and everything he had, with all Israel accompanying him, and brought them up to the Valley of Achor.
Joshua said to him, “Why have you brought trouble on us? May the Lord bring trouble on you today!” Then all Israel stoned him and everything he had, and burned them with fire.
They raised a heap of large stones over him, which remains to this day. The Lord turned from his fierce anger. Therefore that place has been called the Valley of Achor to this day.

The Lord said to Joshua, “Do not be afraid or terrified. Take all the people with you and wage war. Get up and go up to Ai, because I have handed over to you the king of Ai, his people, his city, and his land.
Do to Ai and its king as you did to Jericho and its king. But you may take its plunder and livestock for yourselves. Set an ambush behind the city.”
Joshua and all the fighting men set out to go up to Ai. Joshua chose three thousand mighty warriors and sent them out at night.
He commanded them, saying, “See that when you lie in ambush against the city, behind it, you do not go too far from the city. All of you must be ready.
I and the people with me will approach the city. When they come out to meet us as before, we will flee from them.
They will come out of the city after us and pursue us, because they will say, ‘They are fleeing from us as before.’ We will indeed flee from them.
Then you must rise from your ambush and destroy the city, and the Lord your God will hand it over to you.
When you capture the city, burn it with fire. Act according to the LORD’s word. See to it: I have commanded you.
Joshua sent them out, and they went to the ambush site and took up their position between Bethel and Ai, west of the city. Joshua spent that night among the people.
Joshua rose early in the morning and counted the people. He and the elders of Israel went up to Ai ahead of the people.
All the warriors who were with him went up and approached the city. They camped north of Ai, with a valley between them and Ai.
Joshua took five thousand men and stationed them in ambush between Bethel and Ai, west of the city.
He positioned his people and his entire camp north of the city, with the rear guard west of the city. Joshua went among the people that night.

When the king of Ai saw this, he hurried, and the men of the city rose and went out to meet Israel. All the people of Ai were in the plain, but the people did not know that an ambush had been set for them behind the city.
Joshua and all Israel scattered before them, fleeing along the road to the wilderness.
All the people of Ai raised a shout to pursue them. They pursued Joshua and emptied the city.
Not a man remained in Ai or Bethel who did not go out after Israel. They left the city open and pursued Israel.
The LORD said to Joshua, “Raise the spear in your hand toward Ai, for I have delivered it into your hands.” Joshua raised the spear he held in his hand toward the city.
The men in ambush rose quickly from their position and ran swiftly as he moved his hand. They entered the city and captured it, and they hurried to burn the city with fire.

The men of Ai turned around and saw the smoke of their city rising to the sky. They were unable to flee in either direction, and the people of Israel, who had been fleeing into the wilderness, turned against their pursuers.
Joshua and all Israel saw that the men in ambush had captured the city and that smoke was rising from it. They turned back and struck down the men of Ai.
The others came out of the city to meet them, so the men of Ai were caught in the middle of Israel, with some on one side and some on the other. They struck them down and left them no survivor.
They captured the king of Ai alive and brought him to Joshua.

Israel finished killing all the inhabitants of Ai in the fields and in the wilderness where they had pursued them. They all fell by the sword until they were completely destroyed. Then all Israel returned to Ai and put it to the sword.
All who fell that day, men and women, numbered twelve thousand—all the people of Ai.
Joshua did not lower the hand he had raised with the spear until he had destroyed all the inhabitants of Ai.
The Israelites took only the livestock and the plunder of that city for themselves, according to the LORD’s word, as he had commanded Joshua.
Joshua burned Ai and made it a permanently ruined mound, as it remains to this day.

He hung the king of Ai on a tree until evening. When the sun set, Joshua gave orders, and they took the corpse down from the tree and threw it at the entrance to the city gate. They raised a heap of large stones over him, which remains to this day.
Then Joshua built an altar to the LORD, the God of Israel, on Mount Ebal.

He built it as Moses, the LORD’s servant, had commanded the Israelites, as written in the Book of the Law of Moses: an altar of whole stones on which no iron tool had been used. They offered whole burnt offerings to the LORD on it and sacrificed sacrifices.
There, on these stones of the altar, he wrote a copy of the law of Moses, which he wrote in the presence of the Israelites.

All Israel, with their elders, scribes, and judges, stood on either side of the ark, facing the priests and Levites who carried the ark of the LORD’s covenant. Half of them faced Mount Gerizim, and half faced Mount Ebal, as Moses, the LORD’s servant, had previously commanded for blessing Israel.
Afterward Joshua read all the words of the law, the blessings and the curses, everything written in the Book of the Law.
Joshua did not leave unread a single word of everything Moses had commanded. He read it before the whole assembly of Israel, before the women, the children, and the foreigners living among them.

When all the kings beyond the Jordan—in the hill country, in the plains, and along the entire coast of the Great Sea facing Lebanon—the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, heard,
they gathered together with one accord to wage war against Joshua and Israel.
The inhabitants of Gibeon heard what Joshua had done to Ai and Jericho.
They too acted cunningly. They went and prepared provisions, putting worn-out sacks on their donkeys, along with wineskins that were old, torn, and tied up.
They wore worn-out, patched sandals on their feet and old clothes. The bread they had brought for provisions had dried out and become moldy.
They came to Joshua at the camp at Gilgal and said to him and to the people of Israel, “We have come from a distant country. Now make a treaty with us.”
The Israelites said to the Hivites, “If you live among us, why should you receive a pledge from us?”
They said to Joshua, “We are your servants.” Joshua said to them, “Where are you from, and where have you come from?”
They said to him, “Your servants have come from a land and a country very far away because of the name of the LORD your God, for we have heard of his fame and everything he did in Egypt,
and everything he did to the two kings of the Amorites beyond the Jordan—to Sihon king of Heshbon and Og king of Bashan, who lived at Ashtaroth.”
Our elders and all the inhabitants of our land told us, “Take provisions for the journey and go to meet them. Tell them, ‘We are your servants. Now give us a pledge.’”
They said to Joshua, “This bread of ours was still warm when we took it from our homes as provisions on the day we set out to come to you. But now, look, it has dried out and become moldy.

These wineskins were new when we filled them, but look, they have torn. These clothes and sandals of ours were new when we took them with us, but look, they have worn out because the journey was so very long.”
The men took these provisions of theirs and went away, but they did not ask the LORD for guidance.
Joshua made peace with them and made a treaty with them to spare their lives, and the leaders of the congregation swore an oath to them.
Three days after he had made the treaty with them, they heard that they were their neighbors and lived among them.
The Israelites set out and reached their towns on the third day. The names of their towns were Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth [?], and Kiriath-jearim [?].
The Israelites did not kill them, because the leaders of the congregation had sworn an oath to them by the LORD, the God of Israel. The whole congregation grumbled and argued against the leaders.
The leaders of the congregation said, “We have sworn an oath to them by the LORD, the God of Israel. Now we cannot harm them.
Instead, this is what we will do: we will let them live, so that wrath will not come upon us because of the oaths we swore to them.”

The leaders said to the Israelites, “Let them live, and let them gather wood and draw water for the whole congregation.” So they became wood gatherers and water carriers for the whole congregation, just as the leaders had told them.
Joshua summoned them and said to them, “Why did you deceive us and tell us, ‘We are very far from you,’ when you actually live among us?”
“From now on you are cursed, and there will always be someone among you gathering wood and drawing water for the house of God.”

They answered Joshua, “Your servants were clearly told what the LORD your God commanded his servant Moses: to give you the whole land and to destroy all its inhabitants before you. We feared greatly for our lives, and so we did this.
Now, here we are in your hands. Do to us whatever seems good to you.”
He did this for them: he rescued them from the hands of Israel and did not kill them.
That very day Joshua made them wood gatherers and water carriers for the congregation and for the altar of the LORD, to this day, at the place the LORD chooses.

When Adoni-zedek king of Jerusalem heard that Joshua had captured Ai and destroyed it, and that he had done to Ai and its king just as he had done to Jericho and its king, and that the inhabitants of Gibeon had made peace with Israel and were living among them,
They were very afraid, because Gibeon was a great city, like one of the royal cities. It was larger than Ai, and all its men were mighty warriors.
Adoni-zedek king of Jerusalem sent to Hoham king of Hebron, Piram king of Jarmuth, Japhia king of Lachish, and Debir king of Eglon, sending them this message:
“Come up to me and help me, and let us fight against Gibeon, because it has made peace with Joshua and Israel.”

The five kings of the Amorites—the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Eglon—gathered and went up with all their armies. They camped against Gibeon and made war on it.
The men of Gibeon sent to Joshua at the camp in Gilgal and said to him, “Do not abandon your servants, because all the kings of the Amorites who live in the hill country have gathered against us.”
Joshua went up from Gilgal, with all the fighting men who were with him and all the mighty warriors.
The Lord said to Joshua, “Do not be afraid of them, because I have handed them over to you. Not one of them will be able to stand against you.”
Joshua came upon them suddenly, having marched up from Gilgal all night.

The Lord threw them into confusion before Israel, and the Israelites inflicted a great defeat on them at Gibeon of Beth-horon. They pursued them along the road up to Beth-horon and struck them down as far as Azekah and Makkedah.

As they fled before Israel and were going down the descent of Beth-horon, the Lord hurled large stones from heaven upon them as far as Azekah, and they died. More died from the hailstones than the Israelites killed with the sword.

Then Joshua spoke before the Lord on the day when the Lord handed the Amorites over to Israel. Joshua said in the presence of the Israelites, “Sun, stand still over Gibeon, and you, moon, over the valley of Aijalon.”

The sun stood still, and the moon stopped, until the people had taken vengeance on their enemies. This is written in the Book of Praises. The sun stopped in the middle of the sky and did not hurry to set for about a whole day.
There was no day like that one, either before it or after it, when the Lord listened to Joshua's voice, because the Lord was fighting for Israel.
Joshua and all Israel with him returned to the camp at Gilgal.
These five kings fled and hid in the cave at Makkedah.
Joshua received word, and they told him, “These five kings have been found hiding in the cave at Makkedah.”
Joshua said, “Roll large stones and place them against the entrance of the cave, and leave men there to guard them.
But you must not stop. Pursue your enemies and overtake them. Do not let them enter the city, because the Lord your God has handed them over to you.”

When Joshua and the Israelites had finished inflicting a great slaughter on them, until they were destroyed and not a survivor remained among them, they brought those rebels of Gibeon into their fortified city.
Then all the people returned safely to Joshua at the camp in Makkedah, and no one spoke against any of the Israelites.
Joshua said, “Open the entrance of the cave and bring these five kings out of the cave to me.”
They did as Joshua told them and brought the five kings out of the cave to him: the king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, and the king of Eglon.

When they brought these kings out to Joshua, Joshua called all the military commanders who had gone with him and said to them, “Come forward and put your feet on the necks of these kings.” They came forward and put their feet on the necks of these kings.
Joshua said to them, “Do not be afraid or dismayed. Be strong and courageous, because this is what the Lord will do to all your enemies whom you fight.”
Afterward Joshua killed them and hung them on five trees. They remained hanging on the trees until evening.

At sunset Joshua gave orders, and they took the hanging bodies down from the trees and threw them into the cave where they had hidden. They placed large stones over the entrance of the cave, which remain to this day.
Joshua captured Makkedah that day and struck it with the sword. He killed its king and everyone in it, leaving no survivor. He did to the king of Makkedah as he had done to the king of Jericho.
Joshua, with all Israel accompanying him, went from [?] to Libnah and fought against Libnah.

The Lord also handed it over to Israel, and they destroyed it, its king, and everyone in it with the sword. He left no survivor in it, and Joshua did to its king as he had done to the king of Jericho.
Joshua and all Israel with him moved on from Libnah to Lachish, camped against it, and fought against it.
The Lord handed Lachish over to Israel. Joshua captured it on the second day and destroyed it and everyone in it with the sword, just as he had done to Libnah.
Then Harmon king of Gezer came up to help Lachish. Joshua destroyed him and his people with the sword as well, leaving him no survivor.
Joshua and all Israel with him moved on from Lachish to Eglon, camped against it, and fought against it.
He captured it that day and destroyed it and everyone in it with the sword, just as he had done to Lachish.
Joshua and all Israel with him went up from Eglon to Hebron and fought against it.

He captured it and destroyed it, its king, all its towns, and everyone in it with the sword. He left no survivor among them, just as he had done to Eglon and all the people in it, whom he had destroyed.
Joshua and all Israel with him turned back toward Debir and fought against it.

He captured it, its king, and all its towns, and destroyed them with the sword. He destroyed everyone in it and left no survivor among them. As he had done to Hebron, so he did to Debir and its king, and as he had done to Libnah and its king.

Joshua devastated the whole land—the hill country, the south, the plain, and Ashdod—and all their kings. He left no survivor among them and destroyed all their forces, just as the Lord, the God of Israel, had commanded him.
Joshua destroyed them from Rekem-Gaya to Gaza, including the whole land of Goshen, as far as Gibeon.
Joshua captured all these kings and their territories in a single campaign, because the Lord, the God of Israel, was with him, and he was the one fighting for Israel.
When Nabin king of Hazor heard this, he sent word to Jobab king of Merom, to the king of Shimron, and to the king of Achshaph,
and to the kings north of him, in the hill country, in the south, in the plain of Chinnereth and its plains, and in Naphoth-dor to the west,
and to the Canaanites in the east and west, the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites in the hill country, and the Hivites below Mount Hermon in the land of [?].
They came out with all their armies, as numerous as the sand on the seashore, with a very great number of horses and chariots.
All these kings gathered and camped together by the waters of Merom, preparing to wage war against Israel.
The Lord said to Joshua, “Do not be afraid of them, because tomorrow at this time I will make them all lie slain before the Israelites. Destroy their horses and burn their chariots with fire.”
Joshua came suddenly to the waters of Merom, he and all the fighting men who were with him, and they attacked them.

The Lord handed them over to Israel. They struck them down and pursued them as far as Greater Sidon, as far as the place where the waters gather, and as far as the valley of Mizpeh to the east. They destroyed them, and he left no survivor among them.
Joshua did to them as the Lord had told him: he destroyed their horses and burned their chariots with fire.
At that time Joshua turned back and captured Hazor and killed its king with the sword, because Hazor had formerly been the head of these kingdoms.
He destroyed everyone in it with the sword and left no one breathing among them. He burned Hazor with fire.
Joshua captured all the cities of these kings and their kings, and destroyed them with the sword, just as Moses, the servant of the Lord, had commanded him.
Israel burned all the towns standing on hills, and Joshua burned Hazor.

The Israelites took all the plunder of these cities and the livestock for themselves. They struck down all the people with the sword until they had destroyed them completely, leaving no one breathing among them.
Just as the LORD commanded Moses his servant, so Moses commanded Joshua, and so Joshua did. He left nothing undone of all that the LORD had commanded Moses.
Joshua took all this hill country, all the south, all the land of the plain, all the mountains, and their valleys.
From the mountain that divides and rises toward Seir as far as Gadgad in the valley of Lebanon beneath Mount Hermon, Joshua subdued all their kings and killed them.
Joshua waged war against all these kings for many days.

No town remained that was not handed over to the Israelites and destroyed by them, except the Hivites living in Gibeon. Joshua kept them alive and left them to serve Israel. Joshua captured all these kingdoms and destroyed them.

For it was the LORD who caused their hearts to become bold enough to go out to war against Israel, so that they would be destroyed and no plea for mercy would be made for them, but that they would be wiped out, as the LORD had commanded Moses.

At that time Joshua came and destroyed the giants in the hill country, from Hebron, Debir, and Gebal, and from all the hill country of Judah and all the hill country of Israel. Joshua destroyed them along with their cities.
Not a man remained in the land of the Israelites, except those who remained in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod.
Joshua took the whole land, as the LORD had told Moses, and Joshua gave it to Israel as an inheritance, apportioned among their tribes. And the land rested from war.

These are the kings of the land whom the Israelites destroyed and whose territories they took possession of beyond the Jordan to the east, from the Arnon stream to Mount Hermon, including the whole eastern plain:

Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon and ruled from Aroer [?], on the bank of the Arnon stream, including the middle of the stream valley and half of Gilead, as far as the Aphek stream, the border of the Ammonites;
And the plain as far as the Sea of Chinnereth on the east, and as far as the sea of the plain, the Salt Sea, east of the road to Beth-jeshimoth, and southward beneath the slopes of the highlands.
and the territory of Og king of Bashan, of the family of the giants, who lived in Ashtaroth and Edrei.
He ruled over Mount Ashimon, Salecah, and all Bashan as far as the border of En-dor and Maacah, and over half of Gilead and the territory of Sihon king of Heshbon.
Moses, the servant of the LORD, killed him and gave it as an inheritance to Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.

These are the kings of the land whom Joshua and the Israelites destroyed beyond the Jordan to the west, from Gilgal in the valley of Lebanon to the mountain that divides and rises toward Seir. Joshua gave it to the tribes of Israel as an inheritance according to their allotted portions:
in the mountains, the valleys, the Arabah, Ashdod, the wilderness, and the south—the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
These are the kings of the land whom Joshua destroyed: the king of Jericho, one; the king of Ai, beside Bethel, one;
One king of Jerusalem; one king of Hebron.
the king of Jarmuth, one; the king of Lachish, one;
the king of Eglon, one; the king of Gezer, one;
the king of Debir, one; the king of Hormah, one;
the king of Geder, one; the king of Eder, one;
the king of Libnah, one; the king of Adullam [?], one;
the king of Maqar, one; the king of Bethel, one;
the king of Tappuah, one; the king of Hepher, one;
the king of Aphek, one; the king of Nashron, one;
the king of Madon, one; the king of Hazor, one;
One king of Shimron and Meron; one king of Achshaph.
One king of Taanach; one king of Megiddo.
One king of Rekem; one king of Nekmeam and Carmel.
One king of Dor and Naphath-dor; one king of the valley and Gilgal.
One king of Tirzah. All the kings whom Joshua destroyed numbered thirty-one.
Joshua was old and advanced in years, and the LORD said to him, “You have grown old and advanced in years, and very much land remains to be taken into possession.
This is the land that remains: all the region of the Philistines and all the territory of Endor,

from Shihor, which is east of Egypt, to the boundary of Ekron on the north, which is reckoned as belonging to the Canaanites; the five rulers of the Philistines—the Gazites, Ashdodites, Ashkelonites, Gittites, and Ekronites—and the Avvim
in the south; all the land of the Canaanites, and Mearah of the Sidonians, as far as Aphek and the boundary of the Amorites;
the land of Gebal and all Lebanon toward the sunrise, in Gilead below Mount Hermon, as far as the entrance to Hamath.

All the inhabitants of the mountains, as far as the region of the hot springs, and all the Sidonians—I, the LORD, will destroy them before the Israelites. Only, however, [?] the land of Israel, as I commanded you.
Divide this land into inheritances for the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh with them.
For Reuben, Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh have received their inheritance, which Moses gave them beyond the Jordan to the east, just as my servant Moses gave it to them:
from Aroer, which is on the bank of the Arnon Valley, and the town in the middle of the valley, and all the plain to the west, as far as Ribon;
all the towns of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon, as far as the boundary of the Ammonites;
Gilead, the territory of Endor and Kuros, all Mount Hermon, and all Bashan as far as Salecah;
the whole kingdom of Og in Bashan, who reigned in Ashtaroth and Edrei. He was left from the remnant of the giants whom Moses killed, and they took possession of their land.
But the Israelites did not destroy the peoples of Endor and Kuros, and the Endorites and Kurosites have lived among the Israelites to this day.
Only to the tribe of Levi did he give no allotment, because the offerings of the LORD, the God of Israel, are their inheritance, as Moses told them.
Moses gave an inheritance to the tribe of Reuben according to their clans.
Their territory extended from Aroer, beside the bank of the Arnon Valley, and the town in the middle of the valley, and all the plain as far as Riba;
Heshbon and all the towns in the plain, Ribon, Matbaal, and Beth-bene-ammon;
Jahaz, Karmoth, and Anath;
Kiriathaim, Shemama, Jezereth, and Seir, which is on the mountain in the valley;
Beth-peor, Ashtaroth, Pisgah, and Beth-jeshimoth.

And all the towns in the plain and the entire kingdom of Sihon, king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon. Moses and the Israelites killed him in Midian, along with his chiefs: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba, these five rulers under Sihon who lived in the land.
The Israelites also killed Balaam son of Beor, the diviner, with the sword, along with those they killed.
The boundary of the descendants of Reuben was the Jordan. This was the inheritance of the descendants of Reuben according to their clans: the towns and their surrounding lands.
Moses gave an inheritance to the tribe of Gad, to the descendants of Gad according to their clans.
Their territory included Jazer, all the towns of Gilead, and half the land of the Ammonites, as far as Aroer, which is opposite Rabbah.
It extended from Heshbon to Ramath-mizpeh and Betonim, and from Mahanaim to the boundary of Debir.

In the valley it included Beth-haram, Beth-nimrah, Succoth, Zaphon, and the rest of the kingdom of Sihon, king of Heshbon. Their boundaries extended to the Jordan and to the end of the Sea of Chinnereth, on the eastern side of the Jordan.
This was the inheritance of the descendants of Gad according to their clans: the towns and their surrounding lands.
Moses gave an inheritance to the half-tribe of Manasseh, and it became the portion of the descendants of Manasseh according to their clans.
Their territory extended from Mahanaim and included all Bashan, the entire kingdom of Og king of Bashan, and all the villages of Jair in Bashan—sixty towns.

Moses gave half of Gilead, Ashtaroth, and Edrei, the towns of Og's kingdom in Bashan—these towns and their villages—to the descendants of Machir son of Manasseh, to half the descendants of Machir according to their clans.
Moses gave an inheritance to these two tribes and the half-tribe in the plain of Moab, on the eastern side of the Jordan.
But Moses gave no inheritance to the tribe of Levi, because the LORD, the God of Israel, is their inheritance, as he told them.

These are the inheritances that the Israelites received in the land of Canaan, which Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the ancestral families of the tribes of Israel assigned to them.
Their inheritance was assigned by lot, as the LORD commanded through Moses that it should be given to the nine tribes and the half-tribe.
For Moses had given an inheritance to the two tribes and the half-tribe beyond the Jordan, but he gave the Levites no inheritance among them.
For the descendants of Joseph formed two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim. He gave the Levites no portion in the land except towns to live in and surrounding lands for their livestock and possessions.
The Israelites did as the Lord had commanded Moses, and they divided the land.
The descendants of Judah approached Joshua at Gilgal, and Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite said to Joshua, "You know what the LORD said to Moses his servant about you and me at Kadesh-barnea.
I was forty years old when Moses, the servant of God, sent me from Kadesh-barnea to spy out the land, and I brought him back a report according to what was in my heart.
Our brothers who went up with us frightened the people, but I followed the LORD my God wholeheartedly.
Moses swore at that time, saying, 'The land on which your foot has trodden will be an inheritance for you and your children forever, because you have followed the LORD God wholeheartedly.'

Now, look, the LORD has given us rest, as he said. It has been forty-five years since the LORD spoke this word to Moses, to lead Israel through the wilderness. And now, today, I am eighty-five years old.
Even now I am as strong as I was on the day Moses sent me. My strength now is the same as it was then, for battle and for going out and coming in.

Now give me this hill country that the LORD spoke of that day. You heard that day that there are giants there, and that the cities are large and fortified. Perhaps the LORD will be with me, and I will destroy them, as the LORD said."
Joshua blessed Caleb son of Jephunneh and gave him the fortified city of Hebron as an inheritance.
For this reason, the fortified city of Hebron has been the inheritance of Caleb son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite to this day, because he followed the LORD, the God of Israel, wholeheartedly.
The city of Hebron was formerly called Kiriath-arba of the giants. And the land rested from war.
The allotment for the tribe of Judah, according to their clans, lay along the border of Edom, as far as the wilderness of Zin, to the farthest southern region.
Their boundary ran south of the end of the Salt Sea and went up from there to the bay facing south.
It went out southward to the ascent of Akrakam, passed through Zin, and went up south of Rekem of the valley. It passed through Hazeroth, went up to Addar, and turned toward Karka.
It passes through Azmon and goes out to the Wadi of Egypt, and the boundary ends to the west. This shall be your southern boundary.
The eastern boundary was the end of the Salt Sea as far as the end of the Jordan. The boundary on the northern side began at the bay of the sea, at the end of the Jordan.
The boundary went up to Laban of the Reubenites.

The boundary went up to Debir from the Valley of Achor, and northward it turned toward Galilee, opposite the ascent of Ramin, south of the ravine. The boundary passed by En-shemesh, and its endpoint was at the spring of Dogel.

The boundary went up to the Valley of Ben-hinnom, along the southern side of the Jebusites—that is, Jerusalem. The boundary went up to the top of the mountain facing the Valley of Ben-hinnom on the west, at the end of the Valley of the Giants.
The boundary turned from the mountaintop toward the spring of the waters of Nephtoah and went out to the peak of Mount Ebron. The boundary turned toward Bela, which is Kiriath-naarin.
The boundary turned westward from Bela toward Mount Seir and passed along the northern side of Mount Naarim, which is Chesalon. It went down to Beth-shemesh and passed southward.
The boundary went out along the northern side of Ekron. It turned toward Shikkeron, passed by Mount Bela, and went out to Jabneel. The boundary ended in the west.
Its western boundary was [?], with its boundaries. This was the boundary surrounding the people of Judah according to their clans.

Joshua gave Caleb son of Jephunneh a portion among the people of Judah, according to the command spoken by the Lord. Caleb said to Joshua, “Give me this Kiriath-arba, belonging to the father of the giants.” And Joshua gave Caleb Kiriath-arba, belonging to the father of the giants, which is Hebron.
There Caleb wiped out the three sons of the giants: Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai, sons of the giants.
From there he went up against the inhabitants of Debir. Debir was formerly called Kiriath-sepher.
Caleb said, “Whoever conquers Kiriath-sepher and destroys it, I will give him my daughter Achsah as his wife.”
Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb’s brother, conquered it, and Caleb gave him his daughter Achsah as his wife.
When she became his wife, she wanted to ask her father for a field as an inheritance. She leaned down from her donkey, and Caleb said to her, “What is it, my daughter?”
She said to him, “Give me a blessing. Since you have given me away in the southern land, give me this water reservoir.” And Caleb gave her the upper reservoir and the lower reservoir.
This was the inheritance of the tribe of Judah according to their clans.
The towns of the tribe of Judah lay along the border of Edom in the south. These are the names of the towns of the people of Judah: Kabzeel, Eder, and Jagur;
Kinah, Jarmonah, and Gadgada;
Kedesh, Hazor, and Nathnin;
Zib, Atlam, and Bealoth;
Hazor, Hadattah, and Kiriath-hezron.
And Amam, Shema, and Moladah;
and Hazar-addah, Heshmon, and Beth-pelet;
and Hazar-shual, Beersheba, and Biriothna;
and Baal, Alin, and Ezem;
and Eltelam, Achsin, and Hormah;
and Ziklag, Marmannah, and Samsallah;
and Lebaoth, Shiloah, and Irmon—all the towns numbered thirty-six, with their villages.
In the lowland: Eshtaol, Zorah, and Ashnah;
and Hoh, En-gahom, Pattuh, and Elam;
and Jarmuth, Adullam, Socoh, and Azekah;
and Shaathin, Azithim, Gathar, and Gathronin—fifteen towns with their villages.
And Zenan, Hadashah, and Migdal-gad;
and Dilean, Mizpeh, and Joktheel;
and Lachish, Azkath, and Eglon;
and Cabbon, Lahmas, and Chitlish;
And Adaroth, Beth-dagon, Naamah, and Naqda: sixteen towns with their surrounding lands.
and Libnah, Ether, and Iphtah;
and Ashan, Ashiah, and Ziklag;
and Keilah, Achzib, and Mareshah—nine towns with their villages.
And Ekron, its dependent towns, and its villages;
from the west, and the whole territory of Ashdod, with their villages;
and Ashdod, its dependent towns, and its villages; and Gaza, its dependent towns, and its villages, as far as the Brook of Egypt, with the Great Sea as the boundary.
And these were in the hill country: Shamir, Jattir, and Socoh;
and Rannah, and Kiriath-sepher, which is Debir;
and Anab, Eshtemoh, and Anim;
and Goshen, Holon, and Giloh—eleven towns with their villages.
And Rib, Rumah, and Ashan;
and Jilum, Beth-tappuah, and Aphek;
and Humtah, Kiriath-arba, which is Hebron, and Zibeon—nine towns with their villages.
And Maon, Carmel, Zib, and Atna;
and Jezreel, Nekmaam, and Zaluah;
and Cain, Gibeah, and Tekna—ten towns with their villages.
And Halhul, Beth-zado, and Gathar;
and Maarath, Beth-anath, and Eltekon—six towns with their villages.
And Rabbath and Kiriath-baal, which is Kiriath-naarin—two towns with their villages.
In the wilderness: Beth-arabah, Middin, and Secacah;
and Jeshan, Ir-mahal, and En-gedi—six towns with their villages.
The descendants of Judah did not destroy the Jebusites who lived in Jerusalem. The Jebusites have lived with the descendants of Judah in Jerusalem to this day.
The allotment for the descendants of Joseph extended from the Jordan near Jericho to the waters of Jericho, east of the wilderness that rises from Jericho as far as the hill country of Bethel.
It went from Bethel to Luz and passed into the territory of Eber and Ataroth.
It descended westward to the territory of the Paltites, as far as the territory of Lower Beth-horon and as far as Geder. Its endpoint was to the west.
The descendants of Joseph, Manasseh and Ephraim, received their inheritance.
This was the boundary of the descendants of Ephraim according to their clans: the boundary of their inheritance ran from Ataroth-addar as far as Upper Beth-horon.
The boundary extended to the west of the northern portion. The boundary turned eastward below Shiloh and passed east of Jaluah.
It descended from Jaluah to Ataroth, Igrath, Pagar, and Jericho.
The boundary goes out from Tappuah to the Jordan and runs to the western boundary of the Kanah Valley, ending in the west. This is the inheritance of the tribe of Ephraim according to their clans.
There were towns set apart for the descendants of Ephraim within the inheritance of the descendants of Manasseh—all these towns with their villages.
They did not destroy the Canaanites who lived in Geder. The Canaanites have lived among Ephraim to this day, and they were subjected to tribute.

Gilead became the allotment of the tribe of Manasseh, because he was Joseph’s firstborn. It belonged to Machir, Manasseh’s firstborn, the father of Gilead, because he was the firstborn and a warrior. Gilead and Bashan belonged to him.

There was also an allotment for the remaining descendants of Manasseh according to their clans: the descendants of Abiezer, Helek, Nashriel, Shupham, Hepher, and Shemida. These were the male descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph, according to their clans.
Zelophehad son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh, had no sons, only daughters. These were the names of his daughters: Mahlah, Yaa, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.

They came before Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the leaders of Israel and said, “The Lord commanded Moses to give us an inheritance among our brothers, and at the Lord’s command he gave us one among our father’s brothers. Now give us an inheritance among our fathers’ brothers.” Joshua gave them an inheritance and a portion among their father’s brothers.
Ten portions fell to Manasseh, besides the land of Gilead and Bashan beyond the Jordan.
For the daughters of Manasseh inherited an inheritance along with their brothers, and the land of Gilead belonged to the remaining sons of Manasseh.
The boundary of the descendants of Manasseh ran from the boundary of Maacath, which is to the right of the inhabitants of En-tappuah.
Their land was in Tappuah and [?], and it formed a boundary for the descendants of Manasseh son of Joseph and for the descendants of Ephraim.

Their boundary went down to the valley of the sea, south of the valley. These towns belonged to Ephraim among the towns of Manasseh. The boundary of Manasseh was north of the valley, and its endpoint was to the west.
The south belonged to Ephraim and the north to Manasseh, and the sea was their boundary. They bordered Asher on the north and Issachar on the east.
Manasseh had, opposite Issachar, Beth-shean and its villages, Ibleam and its villages, Endor and its villages, Taanach and its villages, and Megiddo and its villages: three districts.
The Israelites did not destroy these towns, because the Canaanites were determined to live in these towns.
When the Israelites grew strong, they subjected the Canaanites to tribute, but they did not destroy them.
The descendants of Joseph said to Joshua, “Why have you given us only one portion and one tract as an inheritance, when we are a numerous people, since the Lord has blessed us up to this time?”

Joshua said to them, “If you are a numerous people, go up to the forest in the hill country and clear land for yourselves there in the land of the Perizzites and the giants, since the hill country of Ephraim is too cramped for you.”

The descendants of Joseph said, “The hill country and the towns of the Perizzites are not enough for us, because the Canaanites live in the valley land, in Beth-shean and its villages, and in the Valley of Jezreel.”
Joshua said to the house of Joseph, to the descendants of Ephraim and Manasseh, “You are a numerous people and have great strength, but one portion is enough for you.”

“Clear the hill country for yourselves, and it will be enough for you. The slopes of the hill country will be your boundaries. Destroy the Canaanites and the Perizzites, because they have large, strong iron chariots and are strong.”
The whole congregation of the Israelites gathered at Shiloh and set up the tent of meeting there. The land had been subdued before them.
There remained seven tribes among the Israelites whose inheritance had not been divided among them.
Joshua said to the Israelites, “How long will you delay going in to take possession of the land that the Lord, the God of your ancestors, has given you?”
“Choose three men from each tribe, and I will send them out. They are to set out, travel through the land, write a description of it according to their inheritance, and come back to me.”
“They are to divide the land into seven portions. Judah is to remain within its territory in the south, and the house of Joseph is to remain within its territory in the north.”
“You are to describe the land in seven portions and bring the description here to me, and I will show you the portion chosen before the Lord our God.”

“For the Levites have no share among you, because the priesthood of the Lord is their inheritance. Gad, Reuben, and the half-tribe of Manasseh have received their inheritance beyond the Jordan to the east, which Moses, the servant of the Lord, gave them.”

The men set out and went, and Joshua instructed those who went to describe the land, saying to them, “Go, travel through the land and write a description of it. Then come back here to me, and I will cast lots for your portions before the Lord at Shiloh.”
The men went and traveled through the land. They recorded its towns in seven portions on a scroll and came to Joshua at the city of Shiloh.
They cast lots for them at Shiloh before the Lord, and there Joshua divided the land into portions for the Israelites.
The lot for the tribe of the descendants of Benjamin came up according to their clans. The boundary of their inheritance lay between the descendants of Judah and the descendants of Joseph.
Their boundary on the northern side began at the Jordan. The boundary went up along the northern side of Jericho, then went westward up into the hill country, ending at the wilderness of Beth-aven.
From there the boundary passes to Luz, along the southern side of Luz, which is Bethel. The boundary descends to Ataroth-addar, on the hill south of Lower Beth-horon.

The boundary turned along the western side southward from the mountain facing Beth-horon on the south, and ended at Kiriath-baal, which is Kiriath-[?], a city of the descendants of Judah. This was the western side.
The southern side began at the edge of Kiriath-[?]. The boundary went westward and continued to the spring of the waters of Naphtali.

The boundary went down to the end of the mountain facing the Valley of Ben-hinnom, which is in the Valley of the Giants to the north. The boundary of Ben-hinnom went down along the southern side of the Jebusites and descended to En-[?].
It faces north and goes out to En-shemesh, then goes out to Geliloth opposite the ascent of Ramin, and descends to Laban and to Bohan, Reuben’s son.
It passes along the side facing the valley to the north and descends into the valley.
The boundary passed along the northern side of Beth-hoglah, and the boundary ended at the northern tongue of the Salt Sea, at the southern banks of the Jordan. This was the southern boundary.
The Jordan formed its boundary on the eastern side. This was the inheritance of the descendants of Benjamin, according to their clans, with its surrounding boundaries.
The towns of the tribe of the descendants of Benjamin, according to their clans, were Jericho, Zebith, Hoglah, and Emek-keziz;
Beth-arabah, Zemaraim, and Bethel;
Avvim, Parah, and Ophrah;
Kephar-umqa, Ophli, and Geba: fourteen towns with their villages.
Gibeon, Ramah, and Beru;
Mizpah, Chephirah, and Mozah;
Rekem, Raphael, and Taralah;
Zela, Gebirah, Jebus—that is, Jerusalem—Gibeath, and Kiriathaim: fourteen towns with their villages. This was the inheritance of the tribe of the descendants of Benjamin, according to their clans.
The second lot fell to the tribe of the descendants of Simeon, according to their clans. Their inheritance was within the inheritance of the descendants of Judah.
They had in their inheritance Beersheba, Sheba, and Moladah.
Hazar-shual, Balah, and Ezem;
Eltolad, Bethel, and Hormah;
Ziklag, Beth-marcaboth, and Hazar-susah;
Beth-lebaoth and Sharuhen: fourteen towns with their villages.
Ain, Rimmon, Ether, and Ashan: four towns with their villages;
and all the villages surrounding these towns as far as Baath Beth-ramah in the south. This was the inheritance of the tribe of the descendants of Simeon, according to their clans.

The inheritance of the descendants of Simeon came from the allotment of the descendants of Judah, because the portion of the descendants of Judah was too large. The descendants of Simeon therefore received an inheritance from their inheritance.
The third lot came up for the descendants of Zebulun, according to their clans. The boundary of their inheritance extended as far as Ashdod.
Their boundary went up westward to Ramath-shual, reached Dabbesheth, and reached the valley opposite Nekmaam.
It turns from Ashdod eastward to the boundary of Chesulloth and Dabathur, goes out to Rabbith, and ascends to Naphia.
From there it passed eastward toward the sunrise, to Gath, Hepher, Ethah, and Kazin, and went out to Rimmon, Methoa, and Avva.
The boundary curved around north of Hannathon and ended at the valley of Kaphtanael.
It extended to Kattath, Nahalal, Shimron, Idalah, and Bethlehem: twelve towns with their villages.
This was the inheritance of the descendants of Zebulun, according to their clans.
The fourth lot fell to the descendants of Issachar, according to their clans.
Their territory included Jezreel, Chesulloth, and Shuim.
And Hapharaim, Shion, and Ahthar.
And Daberath, Kishion, and Ebez.
And Ramath-en, Enim, En-haddah, and Beth-pazzin.
The boundary reached Tabor, Shahazumah, and Beth-shemesh, and their boundary ended at the Jordan: thirteen towns with their villages.
This was the inheritance of the tribe of the descendants of Issachar according to their clans: the towns with their villages.
The fifth lot fell to the tribe of the descendants of Asher according to their clans.
Their territory included Helkath, Hali, Beten, and Achshaph.
And Allammelech, Amad, and Mishal. It reached Carmel on the west, Shihor, and Lebith.
It turned eastward to Beth-dagon and reached Zebulun and the valley of Iphtah-el on the north, and Beth-emek and Neiel, and extended to Cabul on the north.
And to Ebron, Rehob, Hammon, and Kanah, as far as Great Sidon.
The boundary turned toward Ramah and as far as Tyre, the fortified city. The boundary then turned toward Hosah, and it ended on the west, from the valley of Jareb.
And Umka, Aphek, and Rehob: twenty-two towns with their villages.
This was the inheritance of the tribe of the descendants of Asher according to their clans: these towns with their villages.
The sixth lot fell to the descendants of Naphtali according to their clans.
Their boundary ran from Heleph, from Elon, and from Zaanannim, Adami, Nekeb, and Jabneel, as far as Lakkum, and ended at the Jordan.
The boundary turns west to Aznoth-boz and goes out from there to Hukkok. It meets Zebulun on the south, Asher on the west, and Judah at the Jordan on the east.
And among the large cities were Tyre, Sidon, Hammath, Kiriath, and Chinnereth.
And Adamah, Damah, and Hazor.
And Kedesh, Edrei, and En-zur.
And Dion, Migdal-el, Haddum, Beth-anath, and Beth-shemesh: nineteen cities with their villages.
The seventh lot fell to the descendants of Dan according to their clans.
The territory of their inheritance included Zorah, Eshtaol, and the town of Shemesh.
And Shaalabbin, Aijalon, and Nethlah.
And Elon, Timnah, and Ekron.
And Eltekeh, Gibbethon, and Baalath.
And Jehudith, Baal-debak, and Gath-rimmon.
And Me Jarkon and Karkon, as far as the boundary opposite Elath.

The territory of the descendants of Dan extended beyond these places. The descendants of Dan went up and fought against the people of Aino, captured it, and destroyed it with the sword. They took possession of it and settled in it, and they named Aino Dan after their ancestor Dan.
This was the inheritance of the tribe of the descendants of Dan according to their clans: these cities, their villages, and their surrounding lands.
When they had finished taking possession of the land within its boundaries, the Israelites gave Joshua son of Nun an inheritance among them.
At the LORD’s command, they gave him the town he requested, Timnath Serah in the hill country of Ephraim. He built up the town and settled in it.

These are the inheritances that Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the ancestral families of the tribes of Israel distributed by lot at Shiloh before the Lord, at the entrance of the tent of meeting. They finished dividing the land.
The LORD said to Joshua:
“Tell the Israelites: Set aside towns of refuge for yourselves, as I told you through my servant Moses,
so that a killer who kills someone accidentally and unintentionally may flee there. They will serve you as a refuge from the avenger of blood.

He must flee to one of these towns, stand at the entrance to the town gate, and speak before the elders of that town, explaining his case. They must receive him into the town with them and give him a place to live among them.
If the avenger of blood pursues him, they must not hand the killer over to him, because he struck his neighbor unintentionally and had not hated him previously.

He must remain in that town until he stands before the assembly for judgment, and until the death of the high priest serving at that time. Then the killer may return to his home, his town, and the city from which he fled.”

Then they set apart these towns as places of refuge: Rekem in Galilee, in the hill country of Naphtali; Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim; and Kiriath Arba, which is Hebron, in the hill country of Judah.

Beyond the Jordan, east of Jericho, they designated Bezer in the wilderness, situated on the plain, from the tribe of Reuben; Ramoth Gilead from the tribe of Gad; and Golan in Bashan from the tribe of Manasseh.

These were the towns of rescue and refuge for all the Israelites and for the foreigners living among them, so that anyone who killed someone accidentally could flee there and not be handed over to the avenger of blood before standing before the assembly for judgment.
The leaders of the priests and Levites approached Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the ancestral families of the tribes of Israel.
They said to them at Shiloh in the land of Canaan, “The LORD commanded through Moses that you give us towns to live in, along with their pasturelands for our livestock.”
At the LORD’s command, the Israelites gave the Levites these towns and their pasturelands out of their own inheritance.

The lot fell to the clan of Kohath, to the descendants of Aaron the priest among the Levites. They gave them thirteen towns by lot from the tribe of Judah, the tribe of Simeon, and the tribe of Benjamin.
To the remaining descendants of Kohath they gave ten towns from the tribe of Ephraim, the tribe of Dan, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
To the descendants of Gershon they gave thirteen towns by lot from the tribe of Issachar, the tribe of Asher, the tribe of Naphtali, and the half-tribe of Manasseh in Bashan.
To the descendants of Merari, according to their clans, they gave twelve towns from the tribe of Reuben, the tribe of Gad, and the tribe of Zebulun.
The Israelites gave the Levites these towns and their surrounding lands by lot, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
These are the names of the towns they gave from the tribe of Judah and the tribe of Simeon, listed by name.
They belonged to the descendants of Aaron, of the clan of Kohath among the descendants of Levi, because the first lot was theirs.
They gave them Kiriath-arba, named after the father of the giants, which is Hebron in the hill country of Judah, together with the lands surrounding it.
But the fields of the town and the rest of its surrounding lands they gave to Caleb son of Jephunneh as his inheritance.
To the descendants of Aaron the priest they gave Hebron, a town of refuge in cases of killing, with its pasturelands, and Libnah with its pasturelands.
And Jattir with its pasturelands, and Eshtemoa with its pasturelands.
And Holon with its pasturelands, and Debir with its pasturelands.
And Ain with its pasturelands, and Juttah with its pasturelands, and Beth-shemesh with its pasturelands: nine towns from the tribes of Judah and Simeon.
And from the tribe of Benjamin: Gibeon with its pasturelands, and Geba with its pasturelands.
And Anathoth with its pasturelands, and Almon with its pasturelands: four cities.
All the towns of the descendants of Aaron the priest were thirteen, with their pasturelands.
The towns allotted to the clan of the Levites descended from Kohath, those who remained of the descendants of Kohath, were from the tribe of Ephraim.
They gave them Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim, the city of refuge for those who had killed someone, with its pasturelands, and Geder with its pasturelands.
And Kibzaim with its pasturelands, and Beth-horon with its pasturelands: four towns with their pasturelands.
And from the tribe of Dan: Eltekeh with its pasturelands, and Gibbethon with its pasturelands.
And Aijalon with its pasturelands, and Gath-rimmon with its pasturelands: four towns with their pasturelands.
And from the half-tribe of Manasseh: Taanach with its pasturelands, and Gath-rimmon with its pasturelands: two towns with their pasturelands.
All the towns and cities belonging to the clan of the remaining descendants of Kohath were ten, with their pasturelands.

The descendants of Gershon, from the clan of the Levites, received their towns from the half-tribe of Manasseh: Golan in Bashan, a town of refuge for those who had killed someone, with its surrounding lands, and Ashtaroth with its surrounding lands—two towns with their surrounding lands.
And from the tribe of Issachar: Kishion with its pasturelands, and Daberath with its pasturelands.
And Jarmuth with its pasturelands, and En-gad with its pasturelands: four towns with their pasturelands.
And from the tribe of Asher: Mishal with its pasturelands, and Ekron with its pasturelands.
And Helkath with its pasturelands, and Rehob with its pasturelands: four towns with their pasturelands.

And from the tribe of Naphtali: Rekem in Galilee, the city of refuge for those who had killed someone, with its pasturelands, and Hamrud with its pasturelands, and Kartan with its pasturelands: three towns with their pasturelands.
All the towns of the clan of the descendants of Gershon were thirteen towns with their pasturelands.
And from the tribe of Zebulun: Nakah with its pasturelands, and Kartan with its pasturelands.
And Rimmon with its pasturelands, and Jahla with its pasturelands: four towns with their pasturelands.
Their towns were from the tribe of Reuben: Jahaz with its pasturelands.
Four towns with their pasturelands.
And from the tribe of Gad: Ramoth-gilead, the city of refuge for those who had killed someone, with its pasturelands, and Mahanaim with its pasturelands.
And Heshbon with its pasturelands, and Jazer with its pasturelands: four towns with their pasturelands.
These were the towns of the descendants of Merari, according to their clans, who remained from the tribe of the Levites. Twelve towns with their pasturelands fell to them by lot.
All these towns of the Levites were within the inheritance of the Israelites. The towns of the Levites numbered forty-eight, with their pasturelands.
These towns and cities were settled, each town with its pasturelands surrounding it. All these towns and cities were arranged this way.
The Lord gave Israel all the land that he had sworn to give their ancestors. They took possession of it and settled in it.
The Lord gave them rest on every side, as he had sworn to their ancestors. Not one of their enemies could stand against them; the Lord handed all their enemies over to them.
Not one of all the good promises that the Lord had made to the house of Israel failed; they all came true.
Then Joshua summoned the descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
He said to them, “You have kept everything that Moses, the Lord’s servant, told you, and you have obeyed me in everything I commanded you.
You have not abandoned your fellow Israelites throughout these many days, right up to today, and you have kept the commandments of the Lord your God.

Now the Lord God has given your fellow Israelites rest, just as he told them. So turn back and go to your towns and to the land of your inheritance, which Moses, the Lord’s servant, gave you on the east side of the Jordan.

Only be very careful to carry out the commandments and laws that Moses, the Lord’s servant, commanded you: to love the Lord your God, to keep his commandments, to hold fast to him, and to serve him with all your heart and all your soul.”
Joshua blessed them and sent them away, and they went to their towns.

Moses had given land in Bashan to half the tribe of Manasseh, and Joshua had given land to the other half along with their fellow Israelites on the west side of the Jordan. Joshua sent them away, and they went to their towns, and he blessed them.
