He said to them, “Return to your towns and to the land of your inheritance with great wealth, with very many livestock, with silver, gold, bronze, and iron, and with a great abundance of clothing. Share the plunder taken from your enemies with your fellow Israelites.”

The descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh turned back and left the Israelites at Shiloh in the land of Canaan to go to the land of Gilead, the land of their inheritance, which they had received at the Lord’s command through Moses.

They came to Gilgal beside the Jordan, in the land of Canaan. There the descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh built an altar beside the Jordan, an altar impressive in appearance.

The Israelites heard that the descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh had built an altar facing the land of Canaan, at Gilgal beside the Jordan, in the land of the Israelites.
The whole congregation of the Israelites gathered at Shiloh to go to war against them.
The Israelites sent Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest to the descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh in the land of Gilead.
With him they sent ten leaders, one leader from each of the tribes of Israel. These men were commanders of the forces of Israel.
They came to the descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh in the land of Gilead. They spoke with them and said to them,

“This is what the whole congregation of the Lord says: What is this faithlessness you have committed against the God of Israel? You have turned away from following the Lord and built yourselves an altar to break away from the worship of the Lord.
Was the sin of Peor not enough for us? We have not cleansed ourselves of it to this day, and a plague struck the congregation of the Lord.
If you turn away today from the worship of the Lord, tomorrow wrath will fall on the whole congregation of Israel.

But if the land of your inheritance is unclean, cross over to the land of the Lord’s inheritance, where the Lord’s tabernacle stands, and receive an inheritance among us. Do not despise the worship of the Lord or rebel against us by building yourselves an altar besides the altar of the Lord, the God of Israel.

Did you not see how Achan son of Carmi acted deceitfully and took some of what was devoted to destruction, and wrath fell on the whole congregation of Israel? He was only one man, but we all suffered because of his sin.”
The descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh answered Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest and the commanders of Israel’s forces, saying to them:

“The LORD is the God of gods; the God of our gods is the LORD, and he is our God. He knows Israel, and he knows us. If we did this to break away from him or to act wrongly in the worship of the LORD, may he not save us today.
If we built ourselves an altar to turn away from worshiping the LORD, or to offer sacrifices on it or perform some other worship, may the LORD hold us accountable.
Rather, we did this out of fear of him, so that in the future your children would not say to our children, ‘What do you have to do with the LORD, the God of Israel?

Descendants of Reuben and descendants of Gad, the LORD has placed this Jordan as a boundary between us and you. From now on you have no share in the LORD, the God of Israel.’ Then in the future your children would prevent our children from worshiping the LORD.
For this reason we said, “Let us make a place for ourselves and build an altar for ourselves, not for sacrifice and not for an offering.”

Rather, it is to be a witness between us and you and among our generations after us that we and our generations after us serve the LORD before him with our burnt offerings, our sacrifices, and our offerings, in the place the LORD chooses for his name to dwell there, so that in the future your children will not say to our children, ‘You have no share in the LORD.’

We said, ‘When they say this to us and to our generations in the future, they will answer them: Look at the replica of the LORD’s altar that our ancestors made, not for burnt offerings or sacrifices, but to be a witness between us and you.’

Far be it from us to reject the worship of the LORD and turn away from worshiping the LORD by building ourselves an altar for burnt offerings, offerings, and sacrifices apart from the altar of the LORD, the God of Israel, which stands before his tabernacle.”

Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest and the leaders of the congregation, the commanders of Israel’s forces who were with him, heard the words spoken by the descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, and they were pleased.

Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest said to the descendants of Reuben, the descendants of Gad, and the descendants of Manasseh, “Today we know that the LORD is among us, because you have not committed this act of unfaithfulness against the LORD. You have now rescued the Israelites from the LORD’s hand coming against them in anger.”

Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest and the leaders who were with him returned from the descendants of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh, from the land of Gilead to the land of Canaan, to the Israelites, and brought them back a report.
The report pleased the Israelites, and the Israelites blessed God. They no longer spoke of going to war against them to devastate the land inhabited by the descendants of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh.
The descendants of Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh called the altar they had made “The Altar of Witness,” because it was a witness between them that the LORD alone is God.
After many days, the Lord gave Israel rest from all their enemies around them, and Joshua was old and advanced in years.
Joshua summoned all Israel—its elders, its leaders, its judges, and its scribes—and said to them, “I have grown old and am advanced in years.
You have seen everything the LORD your God did to all these nations, which he destroyed before you. The LORD your God is the one who fought your battles.

But see that I have not allotted to you these remaining nations as an inheritance for your tribes, from the Jordan; and all the nations I destroyed and the Great Sea toward the setting sun I have allotted to you.
The LORD your God himself will break them and destroy them before you, and you will inherit their land, as the LORD your God told you.
Only be very strong, and carefully do everything written in the book of the law of Moses, the LORD’s servant. Do not turn from it to the right or to the left.
Do not mix with these nations that remain among you. Do not mention the names of their gods, swear by them, serve them, or bow down to them.
Instead, hold fast to the LORD your God, as you have done to this day.
The LORD has destroyed great and powerful nations before you, and no one has stood against you to this day.
One man among you will chase a thousand, because the LORD your God is with you, and he fights your battles, as he told you.
Be very careful to fear the LORD your God.
But if you turn away and attach yourselves to the remnant of these nations that remain among you, intermarry with them, and mix with them and they with you,

know that the LORD your God will no longer destroy these nations before you. They will become snares and stumbling blocks for you, [?] at your sides and hooks in your eyes, until you perish from the good land that the LORD your God has given you.

As for me, I am now going the way of all the earth. But you know with all your heart and all your soul that not one of all the good things the Lord your God promised you has failed. All of them have come upon you; not one has failed.
And just as all the good things the Lord your God promised you have come upon you, so all the curses will come upon you, until he destroys you from this good land that he has given you.

If you break the covenant of the Lord your God and the commandments you were given, and go and serve other gods and bow down to them, the anger of the Lord your God will burn against you, and you will quickly perish from the good land that he has given you.
Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel at Shechem and summoned the elders of Israel, their leaders, their judges, and their scribes. He stood before the tent of meeting, before God.

Joshua said to all the people, “This is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: Long ago your ancestors lived beyond the River—Terah, the father of Abraham and the father of Nahor—and there they served other gods.
I took your father Abraham from beyond the River and led him throughout the land of Canaan. I multiplied his descendants and gave him Isaac.
To Isaac I gave Jacob and Esau. To Esau I gave Mount Seir as an inheritance, while Jacob and his sons went down to Egypt.
I sent Moses and Aaron and struck the Egyptians, and I performed wonders among them. After that I brought you out.
I brought your ancestors out of Egypt and brought them to the sea. The Egyptians pursued your ancestors with chariots and horsemen to the Red Sea.

Your ancestors cried out to the Lord, and he put darkness between them and the Egyptians. The Lord divided the Red Sea and brought your ancestors through it. He brought the sea upon the Egyptians and covered them. Your own eyes saw what I did to the Egyptians. I brought you into the wilderness, and you lived in the wilderness for many days.
You came to the land of the Amorites who lived beyond the Jordan, and they fought against you. I handed them over to you and destroyed them before you, and you took possession of their land.
Then Balak son of Zippor, king of the Moabites, rose up and fought against Israel. He sent for Balaam son of Beor to curse you.
But I was not willing to listen to Balaam. Instead, I surely blessed you and rescued you from his hands.

You crossed the Jordan and came to Jericho. The men of Jericho fought against you, along with the Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hittites, Girgashites, Hivites, and Jebusites, and I handed them over to you.
I sent hornets ahead of you and destroyed the two kings of the Amorites before you—not by your swords or by your bows.
I gave you a land for which you had not labored and towns you had not built, and you settled in them. Now you eat from vineyards and olive trees you did not plant.”
“Now fear the Lord and serve him with integrity and faithfulness. Remove from your hearts the foreign gods your ancestors served beyond the River and in Egypt, and serve the Lord.

But if serving the Lord seems wrong to you, choose for yourselves today whom you will serve: the gods your ancestors served beyond the River, or the gods of the Amorites in whose land you live. But as for me and my household, we will serve the Lord, who is God.”
All the people answered, “Far be it from us to forsake the Lord and serve other gods!

For the Lord is our God, the one who brought us up from the land of Egypt, from the house of slavery, and performed these great signs before us. He protected us along the whole way we traveled and among all the peoples through whom we passed.
The Lord our God destroyed all these peoples and the Amorites in whose land we live; the Lord destroyed them before us. Therefore we will serve the Lord, because he alone is God, and he is our God.”
Joshua said to the people, “But take care: you may not be able to serve the Lord, because he is a holy God and a jealous God. He will not forgive your offenses and your sins.
If you forsake the Lord and serve other foreign gods of the land, the Lord will turn against you, bringing harm upon you and destroying you after having done good to you.”
The people said to Joshua, “We will have no other worship; we worship the Lord God alone.”
Joshua said to the people, “You are witnesses against yourselves that you have chosen for yourselves to serve the Lord.” They said to him, “We are witnesses.”
Joshua said to them, “Now remove the foreign gods that are among you, and direct your hearts toward the Lord, the God of Israel.”
The people said to Joshua, “We will serve the Lord our God and obey his voice.”
Joshua made a covenant with the people that day and taught them commandments and laws at Shechem.
Joshua wrote these words in the book of the law of God. He took a large stone and set it up under the terebinth tree in the sanctuary of the Lord.

Joshua said to all the people, “Look, this stone will be a witness for us, because it has heard all the words that the Lord spoke to us. It will be a witness against you, so that you do not deny the Lord your God.”
After Joshua had instructed the people, he sent them away, each to his own inheritance.
After these things, Joshua son of Nun, the servant of the Lord, died at the age of one hundred and ten.
They buried him within the territory of his inheritance, at Timnath-serah in the hill country of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.
Israel served the Lord throughout Joshua’s lifetime and throughout the lifetime of the elders who lived on after Joshua and knew the deeds that the Lord had done for Israel.

The bones of Joseph, which the Israelites had brought up from Egypt, they buried at Shechem, in the plot of land that Jacob had bought from Hamor, the father of Shechem, for a hundred ewes. It became an inheritance for Joseph’s descendants.
Eleazar the priest, son of Aaron the priest, died, and they buried him at Gibeah of Phinehas his son, which had been given to him in the hill country of Ephraim.
